mainTopic: רבי שמעון's view of a perforated pot (עציץ נקוב), and the hole sizes that end a כלי חרס's status, including a vessel sealed with a צמיד פתיל
overview: This amud opens with the end of a challenge. רבי שמעון said a perforated pot differs from an unperforated one regarding הכשר זרעים, which suggests he sees it as attached to the ground. The answer is that for all matters he treats it as detached, and טומאה of seeds is a special exception based on a פסוק. Next, an elder asks רבי זירא about a root lined up with the hole. רבי זירא stays silent, and later says something the elder finds obvious, so אביי offers a corrected version: a hole below the level of a רביעית. רבא then lists five hole sizes in a כלי חרס, each removing a different legal status. He adds that a vessel sealed with a צמיד פתיל keeps its status until most of it breaks. רב אסי reports a pomegranate-sized hole, and רבא limits that to a sealed vessel. The גמרא objects that this contradicts רבא's own rule, and begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The challenge ends: was רבי שמעון's rule only about preparing seeds?
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a challenge that began on the previous amud. It quotes רבי שמעון saying that the only difference between a perforated and an unperforated pot is in הכשר זרעים. This suggests that in that area he treats a perforated pot as attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: …rather, only regarding making seeds susceptible to impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the last words of a challenge from the previous section. The challenger cites רבי שמעון saying that perforated and unperforated pots differ only in הכשר זרעים, so in that area he seems to treat a perforated pot as attached to the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון distinguishes a perforated pot from an unperforated one for seeds, he seems to view the perforated pot as connected to the ground. That clashes with his ruling that someone who plucks from a perforated pot on שבת is exempt, which treats it as detached. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: To make something susceptible (able to become טמא)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the END of a question. Its beginning is on the previous part of the דף, so don't look for the full question here.

phrases.english: Rather, only regarding rendering seeds susceptible [to impurity]!
phrases.notes: Conclusion of a challenge that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge begun in the previous section of the דף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The understanding of רבי שמעון's view on a perforated pot (עציץ נקוב).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון says perforated and unperforated pots differ in הכשר זרעים. That implies he treats a perforated pot as attached, which contradicts his exempting someone who plucks from it on שבת as if it were detached.

steps.title: Generally detached; טומאה of seeds is a special exception
steps.stepSummary: The answer: for all matters, רבי שמעון treats a perforated pot as detached. טומאה is different, because the Torah widened purity for seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For all matters, רבי שמעון treats it like something detached. But טומאה is different, because the Torah widened purity for seeds, as it says: 'upon any sowing seed that is sown.'
steps.whatsHappening: The responder says רבי שמעון's basic rule is that a plant in a perforated pot counts as detached for everything. The only exception is טומאה of seeds, where a special פסוק makes them stay pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The category stays the same: in a perforated pot, the plant is treated as detached. But in the area of טומאה, the Torah gives extra purity. The doubled wording 'זרע זרוע' includes any seed that is growing in a sowing-like way, so seeds in a perforated pot are pure. This exception does not change רבי שמעון's general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Like something detached (not attached to the ground)
A sowing seed (the doubled wording teaches extra inclusion)

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains how רבי שמעון can exempt someone who plucks from a perforated pot on שבת (treating it as detached), even though seeds in that pot are treated as pure for טומאה.

phrases.english: He said to him: For all matters,
Rabbi Shimon treats it as detached,
but the matter of impurity is different,
for the Torah amplified purity regarding seeds,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל כׇּל זֶרַע זֵרוּעַ אֲשֶׁר יִזָּרֵעַ״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Upon any sowing seed that is sown' (Leviticus 11:37).
phrases.notes: The repeated root (זרע זרוע) is read as including seeds in a perforated pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְכׇל מִילֵּי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כְּתָלוּשׁ מְשַׁוֵּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by separating the general rule from the טומאה exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a general rule plus a verse-based exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי שמעון distinguishes perforated from unperforated pots regarding seeds, he must consider a perforated pot attached to the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: Generally, רבי שמעון treats a perforated pot as detached. Only regarding טומאה does a פסוק make seeds in it pure.

steps.title: An elder asks about a root lined up with the hole
steps.stepSummary: An elder asks רבי זירא what רבי שמעון would hold if the plant's root sits right over the hole. רבי זירא stays silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder asked רבי זירא: If the root is opposite the hole, what would רבי שמעון say? He was silent and told him nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. An elder asks whether רבי שמעון would agree the plant counts as attached when its root faces the hole directly, and רבי זירא does not answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the root lines up with the hole, the plant seems to draw directly from the ground. So maybe even רבי שמעון would treat it as attached. רבי זירא's silence leaves the question open and sets up the story that follows.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: A certain elder asked Rabbi Zeira:
A root opposite the hole,
what would Rabbi Shimon say?

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי שמעון's general 'detached' rule by asking about an extreme case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון treat a plant as attached when its root lies directly over the hole?

steps.title: רבי זירא later states what רבי שמעון agrees to
steps.stepSummary: The elder later finds רבי זירא teaching that רבי שמעון agrees when the hole is big enough to make the pot טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he found him sitting and saying: And רבי שמעון agrees that if it was perforated enough to make it pure…
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The elder overhears רבי זירא teaching that רבי שמעון agrees the plant counts as attached when the hole is large enough to make the pot טהור. This sets up the elder's complaint in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole 'בכדי טהרתו' is big enough that the pot no longer counts as a vessel (the size where olives fall out). רבי זירא says that in such a case, even רבי שמעון treats the plant as attached to the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: Large enough to make it ritually pure (no longer a vessel)

phrases.english: One time he found him
sitting and saying:
And Rabbi Shimon agrees
that if it was perforated enough to render it pure [it is like attached].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what רבי זירא later said, which the elder will now attack.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון agrees that a pot with a hole large enough to make it טהור is treated as attached to the ground.

steps.title: The elder objects: you could not answer my question, yet you decide a harder case?
steps.stepSummary: The elder complains: you would not answer my real question about the root, yet you decide the case of a hole big enough for purity, where the roots are not even over the hole?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Now, I asked you about a root opposite the hole and you told me nothing. And 'perforated enough to make it pure' needs to be said?!
steps.whatsHappening: The elder challenges רבי זירא's statement. He argues that if the root-over-the-hole case was too unclear to answer, the case of plants not over the hole should be even more unclear, yet רבי זירא decided it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plant whose root sits right over the hole has the strongest claim to count as attached. If רבי זירא could not decide that case, then plants whose roots are not over the hole should be at least as doubtful, yet he declared them all attached. The elder's challenge suggests רבי זירא's statement must have meant something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (opens a 'how much more so' argument)
Is that even a question? (here: it should be even more in doubt)

phrases.english: He said to him: Now,
I asked you about a root opposite the hole
and you did not tell me anything,
[so] perforated enough to render it pure, does that need to be said?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶגֶד נֶקֶב בְּעַאי מִינָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's statement from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's statement that רבי שמעון agrees when the hole is בכדי טהרתו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the easier case of a root over the hole could not be decided, the case of plants not over the hole should be even harder. Deciding it with certainty makes no sense.

steps.title: אביי's corrected version: a hole below a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that if רבי זירא's statement was really said, it was about a hole below the level that holds a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If רבי זירא's statement was said, this is how it was said: And רבי שמעון agrees that if it was perforated below a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fixes the wording of רבי זירא's statement so it is no longer obvious. In his version, the point is about a hole located below the level that holds a רביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hole is low enough that the pot cannot hold a רביעית below it, the pot loses its status as a vessel, even if the hole is small. This is a different case from the one the elder attacked. So the elder's objection no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how it was stated
Below the level holding a רביעית (a quarter-log)

phrases.english: Abaye said: And if it was stated,
this [statement] of Rabbi Zeira,
this is how it was stated:
And Rabbi Shimon agrees
that if it was perforated below [the level of] a quarter-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְאִי אִיתְּמַר לְהָא דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא, הָכִי הוּא דְּאִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the elder's objection by changing the wording of רבי זירא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא spoke about a hole large enough to make the pot טהור, which seemed to decide a harder case than the one he left unanswered.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי זירא spoke about a hole below a רביעית, which removes vessel status even when the hole is small.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי שמעון agrees the plant counts as attached when the hole is low enough that the pot cannot hold a רביעית.

steps.title: רבא's five levels of holes in a clay vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists five hole sizes in a כלי חרס. Each larger hole removes one more legal status from the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are five measures for clay vessels. A hole that lets liquid out makes it pure from shard-impurity, but it is still a vessel for sanctifying מי חטאת. A hole that lets liquid in makes it unfit for מי חטאת, but it can still make seeds susceptible. A hole the size of a small root makes it unable to make seeds susceptible, but it is still a vessel for holding olives. A hole that lets olives out makes it pure as an olive-holder, but it is still a vessel for pomegranates. A hole that lets pomegranates out makes it pure from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is holes in pots, the גמרא brings רבא's list of five hole sizes in a כלי חרס. Each size cancels a specific legal use of the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each law requires a different degree of 'wholeness.' A גיסטרא (usable shard) loses its טומאה with even a tiny leak. מי חטאת need a vessel that does not let liquid in. הכשר זרעים is lost at a root-sized hole. General vessel טומאה depends on what the vessel can still hold: first olives, then pomegranates.

keyTerms.meaning: A usable broken shard of a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: 'Pure from X' (טָהוֹר מִ־) here does not mean the vessel is fully טהור. It means only that specific status is lost, while the vessel can still count for the next, larger use.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'is this still a vessel?' has no single answer. The answer depends on which law you are asking about. This fits the earlier discussion of when a perforated pot stops counting as a vessel.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, חָמֵשׁ מִדּוֹת בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס:
phrases.english: Rava said: There are five measures for earthenware vessels:
If it was perforated enough for liquid to seep out,
it is pure from the impurity of a shard,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין כְּלִי הוּא לְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ מֵי חַטָּאת;
phrases.english: but it is still a vessel for sanctifying purification water in it;
if it was perforated enough for liquid to enter,
it is unfit for sanctifying purification water in it,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין כְּלִי הוּא לְהַכְשִׁיר בּוֹ זְרָעִים;
phrases.english: but it is still a vessel for rendering seeds in it susceptible;
if it was perforated like [the width of] a small root,
it no longer renders seeds in it susceptible,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין כְּלִי הוּא לְקַבֵּל בּוֹ זֵיתִים;
phrases.english: but it is still a vessel for holding olives;
if it was perforated enough for olives to fall out,
it is pure as a vessel for holding olives,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין כְּלִי הוּא לְקַבֵּל בּוֹ רִימּוֹנִים;
phrases.english: but it is still a vessel for holding pomegranates;
if it was perforated enough for pomegranates to fall out,
it is pure from everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, חָמֵשׁ מִדּוֹת בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought in because of the related topic of holes making a clay vessel טהור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are five rising hole sizes in a כלי חרס. Each one cancels a further legal status, until a pomegranate-sized hole makes the vessel fully טהור.

steps.title: Exception: a vessel sealed with a צמיד פתיל
steps.stepSummary: If the vessel has a צמיד פתיל (sealed cover), it keeps its protective status until most of it is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is surrounded by a sealed cover, [it keeps its status] until most of it is broken.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception to his list. A clay vessel sealed with a צמיד פתיל keeps its status even with large holes, until most of it breaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a tent with a dead body, a sealed clay vessel protects what is inside from טומאה. For this protective role, the hole sizes above do not cancel its status. Only when the majority of the vessel breaks does it stop counting.

keyTerms.meaning: Until most of it is broken

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's five hole sizes apply in general. For a vessel with a צמיד פתיל protecting its contents, only breaking most of the vessel ends its status.

phrases.english: And if it was surrounded with a sealed cover,
[it is not pure] until most of it is broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to רבא's five-level list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A clay vessel sealed with a צמיד פתיל keeps its protective status until the majority of it is broken.

steps.title: רב אסי's tradition: a pomegranate-sized hole
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says he heard that the hole size for a כלי חרס is large enough for a pomegranate to fall out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: I heard that for an earthenware vessel, the measure of the hole is big enough to let a pomegranate fall out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי reports a tradition about how big a hole must be in a כלי חרס. He says it is the size of a pomegranate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's list of five sizes (step 7), the smallest hole that ends an ordinary כלי חרס's ability to become טמא was much smaller, the size of an olive. רב אסי's pomegranate size is far bigger, so it seems to clash with that list. The next step deals with this.

keyTerms.meaning: Big enough for a pomegranate to fall out

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
I heard that an earthenware vessel,
its measure is enough to let a pomegranate out.
phrases.notes: This is the hole size that makes it טהור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new tradition with a much larger hole size than the sizes in רבא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי חרס needs a pomegranate-sized hole to become טהור.

steps.title: רבא limits the tradition to a sealed vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב אסי that perhaps his tradition was only about a vessel sealed with a צמיד פתיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Perhaps you only heard this about a vessel whose opening is sealed with a tight cover.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not reject רב אסי's tradition outright. He narrows it so that it applies only to a vessel with a צמיד פתיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps both rules in place. An ordinary כלי חרס still becomes טהור with an olive-sized hole, and the pomegranate size would apply only to a sealed vessel, which keeps protecting what is inside for longer.

keyTerms.meaning: Surrounded by a tightly sealed cover

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Perhaps you did not hear it,
except about a vessel surrounded by a sealed cover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב אסי's tradition so it does not clash with the olive-size rule for ordinary vessels.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying רב אסי's rule to ordinary vessels, but keeps it for sealed ones.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Applying the pomegranate size to every כלי חרס would contradict the olive-size rule.

steps.title: But רבא himself said a sealed vessel needs most of it broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבא himself ruled a sealed vessel keeps its status until most of it is broken, not at a pomegranate-sized hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it רבא himself who said that a vessel sealed with a tight cover keeps its status until most of it is broken?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with his own earlier ruling from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא just placed the pomegranate size on a sealed vessel. However, he himself said a sealed vessel keeps protecting until a majority of it is broken. A pomegranate-sized hole is less than a majority, so his two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: He is the one who said
Until most of it is broken

phrases.english: But isn't Rava the one who said:
a vessel surrounded by a sealed cover
protects until most of it is broken!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's limitation by pointing to his own earlier ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the pomegranate size applies to a sealed vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא said a sealed vessel needs a majority broken, which is more than a pomegranate-sized hole. He cannot hold both.

steps.title: Opening of the answer: this is not difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by saying the contradiction is not a real problem. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line is a setup. The גמרא announces that it can resolve the contradiction, and the actual explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' usually leads into an answer that shows the two rulings are about two different cases. The details of which case is which have not yet appeared on this amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (opens an answer that splits the cases)

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
phrases.notes: The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's two rulings about sealed vessels seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They will be shown to address different cases, as the next passage explains.
